title: 2010 ADA Standards (elevators) and IBC stretcher rule
edition: 2010 ADA Standards §407; IBC 3002.4 as printed in the 2025 California Building Code
notes: Car depth is measured from the back wall to the front return (ADA Table 407.4.1 also gives 54 in to the inside face of the door). The ADA's 36 in door may be 5/8 in (16 mm) narrower. The stretcher rule applies where the elevator serves four or more storeys; the IBC counts storeys above or below the grade plane. The small-lift sizes (408–410) are the inch values converted exactly, since the ADA's metric figures are rounded.

accessible_cars.description: Minimum inside car dimensions, Table 407.4.1, with the door centred, to one side, or anywhere
LULA car at least 42 in wide by 54 in deep (1065 × 1370 mm) with the door on the narrow end at least 32 in (815 mm); or 51 × 51 in (1295 × 1295 mm) with a 36 in (915 mm) door (exception 1)
Private-residence elevator: clear floor at least 36 × 48 in (915 × 1220 mm)
Platform lift: a 30 × 48 in (760 × 1220 mm) clear floor space, end doors at least 32 in (815 mm)

stretcher.description: At least one elevator serving every floor takes a 24 × 84 in (610 × 2134 mm) stretcher, lying flat, corners of at least 5 in (127 mm) radius

landing.description: 30 × 48 in (760 × 1220 mm) clear floor space at the hall call buttons, taken in front of the entrance

call_buttons.description: Hall call buttons between 15 and 48 in (380–1220 mm) above the floor

stairlift.description: A stairway chairlift or inclined platform lift on a stair serving R-3, or within an R-2 dwelling unit, leaves at least 20 in (508 mm) clear passage measured from the folded seat or platform; any other stair keeps its required width (44 in, or 36 in serving fewer than 50 occupants). A 30 × 48 in wheelchair space at each end of a platform lift.
